title: The most beautiful names
hook: to Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call on Him by them (7:180)

segments.voice: Yesterday, camp four closed: seventy-five days from An-Nas back to An-Naba'. Your line was the ones every child knows. Did you say one surah by heart? Today, camp five begins. Day two hundred thirty-two.

Listen to the names of Muslim men you know. Abdullah. Abdul-Rahman. Abdul-Karim. Abdul-Aziz. Abdul-Latif. Every one of them starts the same way, 'abd, servant of, and then comes a name of God. Servant of the Merciful. Servant of the Generous. Servant of the Mighty. Servant of the Gentle. Millions of people walk around carrying a name of God inside their own name, and many never think about it. So every time you've said hi to an Abdul-Rahman, you've said one of the most beautiful names out loud. Camp five is called further in, and it begins with the names. Today: al-asma' al-husna, the most beautiful names.
screen: `ABDULLAH, ABDUL-RAHMAN, ABDUL-KARIM.` → `SERVANT OF A NAME.` → `CAMP FIVE: FURTHER IN.`

segments.voice: The phrase comes straight from the Qur'an. Here is Pickthall's translation of Surah al-A'raf: Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them. Asma' is the plural of ism, name. Husna is the feminine form of ahsan, most beautiful, best, finest. The fairest names. The phrase comes back in other surahs too: at the end of al-Hashr, and in Ta Ha, and in al-Isra', where people are told they may call on Allah or call on the Most Merciful, whichever they call, His are the most beautiful names. Why names, and not a description? Muslims say Allah can't be seen, pictured or fully understood, but He can be known through what He has told people about Himself. Each name is like a window: you can't see the whole house through one window, but you can see something true. The Merciful. The Living. Peace. The Loving. And notice the verb: invoke Him by them, call on Him by them. The names aren't for a list on a wall. They're for calling. A person who is afraid might call on the Protector. A person who has done wrong calls on the Forgiving. Someone lost calls on the Guide. You've met several already. Ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim in every bismillah. Al-Wadud, the Loving, in al-Buruj. Al-Hayy and al-Qayyum in Ayat al-Kursi. For the next weeks we'll take them one at a time, a first selection, and each one will be a new way to call.
screen: `ASMA' — NAMES. HUSNA — MOST BEAUTIFUL.` · `EACH NAME A WINDOW.` · `NAMES ARE FOR CALLING.` · `THE ONES YOU'VE ALREADY MET.` · then, large: `CALL HIM BY HIS NAMES.`

segments.voice: Sit, and settle your breath. Now look for a name of Allah you already know. Maybe ar-Rahman, from the bismillah. Maybe as-Salam, peace, hidden in the greeting. Maybe al-Wadud, the Loving. Pick one. Say it slowly in your mind with each out-breath, and notice what it brings up. A feeling, a memory, a need. If you pray, you can call on Allah by that name, simply: ya Rahman, O Most Merciful. If you don't, just let the name and its meaning sit with you. The bell holds the time.
Al-asma' al-husna. The most beautiful names: the names by which Allah is known in the Qur'an, given to call on Him by. Today's word.
Your line: call him by his names. Today, when you need something, notice which name fits the need, and if you pray, call on Him by it. Day two hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Muslims call on Allah by the name that fits their need in du'a (ya Rahman, ya Ghafur), learn the names as children, often through recited lists, and many carry a name of Allah in their own, as in Abdullah or Abdul-Rahman.

myth: the phrase the most beautiful names comes from the Qur'an
Muslims say the names give a full picture of Allah
each is a window: something true, never the whole.

invoke Him by them: they're for calling.

fork.setup: you've done something wrong and want to turn back. which name would you call on?
fork.reveal: the names are for calling, and people call on the one that fits the need: the Forgiving for a wrong.

trapdoor: what you thought: a list of God's titles.
what it means: names given in the Qur'an so people can know Allah a little and call on Him by them.
what a scholar hears: husna is the feminine elative of hasan; 7:180, 17:110, 20:8, 59:24; many 'abd names follow them.

sources.quoted: Allah's are the fairest names. Invoke Him by them.

sources.ref: Qur'an 17:110; 20:8; 59:24 (His are the most beautiful names)

notes: Please confirm the exact Pickthall wording of the opening of 7:180.
The 'window' image is the writer's teaching device for the idea that the names give true but partial knowledge; a Keeper may prefer a classical framing.
